hints: An interval [a,b] contains [c,d] when a<=c and b>=d.
Sort intervals by start ascending and, for equal starts, end descending.
A left-to-right scan can mark whether an earlier interval contains this one; a right-to-left scan handles whether a later interval is inside it.
analogy: Lay intervals in sorted order so any possible container is encountered before its contained interval.
example: For [1,6] and [2,4], the first contains the second and the second is contained by the first.
algorithm: Sort by (left ascending, right descending). Scan forward with the greatest right endpoint seen to mark contained; scan backward with the smallest right endpoint seen to mark containing. Handle exact duplicates as a group.
correctness: The sort places every strict container before the interval it contains and every contained interval after it; the running endpoint extrema detect the required relation.
complexity: O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
